title: Vesper and the Playlist
premise: Ines Zhou, the statistician for the Vesper High quiz-bowl team, has spent years proving the regional tournament brackets are rigged against their underfunded school — and burying the proof, because 'fine' is safer than furious. When a college essay prompt asks them to describe an injustice they failed to fight, the truth they've hidden spills onto the page, and their best friend Dev reads it, forcing the whole team to decide whether to expose the league or play the rigged game anyway. Ines must lead the team to win a championship that won't count — and then the underground rival league, the one that does — while learning that inheritance means choosing what you carry forward. It ends with Ines submitting the essay, the league's fix exposed by the team's own recorded data, and a prom-night victory that finally feels like theirs.
about_author: Rafael Reyes is a former academic decathlon coach from the Central Valley who writes about smart kids the sports movies forgot. He collects broken calculators and believes every spreadsheet hides a confession.

chapters.title: The Margin of Error
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines runs probability models on the regional quiz-bowl brackets and confirms, for the third year running, the seeding is rigged against Vesper High. They file the finding away in a locked folder instead of speaking up, telling themselves the team can win anyway. Emotional beat: the ache of knowing and staying quiet.

chapters.title: Fine, Obviously
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At practice, Ines deflects Dev's questions about why they've been distant, performing cheerfulness while quietly compiling a dossier on league commissioner Aldous Prine. A flashback shows Ines's mother's own silenced complaint years ago. Emotional beat: inherited silence.

chapters.title: Prompt Two
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. English class reveals the common-app essay prompt: 'Describe a time you witnessed injustice and chose not to act.' Ines freezes; the room fills with easy answers. That night, unable to sleep, Ines opens the locked folder and starts typing the truth. Emotional beat: the dam cracking.

chapters.title: Dev Reads It
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev finds the draft essay open on Ines's laptop while house-sitting and reads every word, including the accusation against Prine. Hurt that Ines never trusted them wars with awe at the evidence. Emotional beat: betrayal and revelation entwined.

chapters.title: The Team Meeting
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev convenes the team — captain Marisol, buzzer prodigy Theo, alternate Priya — and reveals the dossier without Ines's consent. Ines arrives mid-argument, furious and exposed. The team splits: expose Prine now, or win regionals first so the accusation can't be dismissed as sour grapes. Emotional beat: fracture.

chapters.title: Marisol's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol reveals her late father coached Vesper's 1998 team, which lost a rigged final and never spoke of it; his old scorebooks contain the same statistical anomalies. She gives Ines the scorebooks, making the fight an inheritance. Emotional beat: grief converted to purpose.

chapters.title: Playing the Rigged Game
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The team commits to winning regionals within Prine's rigged system, using Ines's models to exploit the bracket's flaws. First-round match montage; Ines learns to trust teammates with the data. Emotional beat: guarded hope.

chapters.title: Prine's Offer
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Prine corners Ines after a match, having heard rumors, and offers a college recommendation letter in exchange for the dossier's destruction. Ines says yes — and hates themselves for it. Emotional beat: the temptation of a clean exit.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines pockets Prine's letter and can't look at Dev. Priya notices Ines's guilt and, without judging, shares her own story of a coach who bought her silence. Emotional beat: complicity recognized.

chapters.title: Semifinals
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's buzzer speed carries the team to the regional final, but he overhears Prine arranging a power outage for the final's deciding round. He tells Ines, who realizes the rigging is escalating. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Final That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The regional final: the lights 'fail' exactly as predicted, but the team, forewarned, has drilled blackout rounds and wins anyway. Victory tastes hollow — the trophy changes nothing, and Prine smiles through it. Emotional beat: triumph and futility in the same breath.

chapters.title: Everything Is Not Fine
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev confronts Ines about the letter; the fight is raw, Dev accusing Ines of becoming what they study. Ines finally says aloud that they were afraid, not fine. They don't reconcile, but the truth is on the table. Emotional beat: the cost of honesty.

chapters.title: The Underground League
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya reveals the Circuit — an unsanctioned league of schools the official one has squeezed out, playing in library basements and rec centers. Its coordinator, a retired referee Prine ruined, offers Vesper a place. Emotional beat: finding the real game.

chapters.title: Learning to Lose
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The Circuit's teams are faster and stranger; Vesper loses their first match badly. Marisol rebuilds the team's identity around Ines's statistics as a shared language rather than a secret. Emotional beat: humility as strength.

chapters.title: Recording Everything
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines designs a plan: win the Circuit championship while logging verifiable data on Prine's rigging, then publish everything — the dossier, the scorebooks, the recordings — to the state board and the press. The team signs on, including a hesitant Dev. Emotional beat: alliance rebuilt on truth.

chapters.title: Prom Complications
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Circuit semifinals fall on prom night; the league refuses to reschedule, calling it a test of priorities. The team chooses the match, but Dev and Ines, still estranged, must plan it together. Emotional beat: awkward tenderness returning.

chapters.title: Prine Strikes Back
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Prine discovers the dossier's existence, gets Ines suspended from the team on a fabricated eligibility violation, and threatens the college recommendation. Ines, alone, almost accepts — then reopens their mother's old complaint letter and finds her signature. Emotional beat: choosing inheritance over fear.

chapters.title: The Alternate Steps Up
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. With Ines suspended, Priya must play the semifinal as statistician and competitor. Ines coaches from the bleachers via coded flashcards. Vesper wins by two points. Emotional beat: the team carrying the person who carried them.

chapters.title: Reinstated
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev and Marisol present the 1998 scorebooks to the school board, forcing Ines's reinstatement and putting Prine's history on public record. Prine escalates: he'll attend the Circuit final personally. Emotional beat: the noose tightening on the villain.

chapters.title: The Championship That Does
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The Circuit final against Prine's favored academy, with Prine watching from the back row. Ines plays, not just calculates — buzzing in on a question about statistical ethics, voice steady. Vesper wins. Emotional beat: earned, unrigged victory.

chapters.title: Everything on the Record
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Climax. That night, Ines uploads the full dossier — scorebooks, recordings, Prine's own letter — to the state board and a journalist, then reads the finished college essay aloud to the team in the empty gym. Prine is suspended pending investigation; the letter he offered Ines is submitted as evidence. Emotional beat: silence finally broken, at last without shame.

chapters.title: Prom, After All
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Resolution. A week late, the team throws its own prom in the library basement where the Circuit began — bad lighting, good music, the trophy used as a punch bowl. Ines and Dev slow-dance and trade the playlist they each made during the fight. Ines's acceptance letter arrives by morning. Emotional beat: joy that belongs entirely to them.
